title: The Last Machine
premise: Xanthe Brightwater, a terraformer on the colony world Vesperine, tends a seed-vault garden intended for a future generation while quietly running contraband messages between two colonies that severed contact decades ago. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream—a countdown, a voice, a door—Xanthe realizes the dormant relay at the edge of dead space has woken and is broadcasting something buried in the colony's founding. Pursued by the Council that wants the dream silenced and shadowed by Ilsa, a courier who knows his smuggling routes better than he'd like, Xanthe races to the relay to learn the truth: the founders deliberately infected the children's sleep with a message of apology and inheritance. In the end, Xanthe must choose between destroying the signal to keep the fragile peace or letting it through, knowing either choice will cost him the only life he built.
about_author: Mara Ravensworth is the pen name of a former agricultural engineer who spent six years designing closed-loop habitats before turning to fiction. She writes science fiction about people who maintain things—gardens, machines, silences—and what it costs when those things finally break.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. He walks the seed-vault terraces at dawn, cataloguing plants no living colonist will eat, then loads contraband letters into his hauler's false panels. The beat is quiet loneliness—the comfort of tending what doesn't yet exist.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. He flies the relay run between Vesperine and its estranged sister colony Meridian, dodging Council scan buoys. A near-miss forces him to jettison a pod. The beat is tension sharpening into routine dread—he's done this too long.

chapters.title: Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. A schoolteacher friend describes forty children drawing the same image: a tower in darkness, numbers counting down. Ilsa, a courier, recognizes the tower from old route maps. The beat is unease—the first crack in normalcy.

chapters.title: What the Council Knows
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Summoned before the Council under pretext of a cargo audit, he notices a sealed file labeled RELAY-0 and a scientist, Dr. Oyelaran, being escorted out in disgrace. The beat is paranoia; he realizes others are afraid too.

chapters.title: The Courier Who Knew
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She confronts Xanthe at a waystation, revealing she's mapped his smuggling runs for years—not to expose him but because her brother vanished near Relay-0 twenty years ago. The beat is wary alliance born of mutual leverage.

chapters.title: Countdown in the Cradle
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. His young neighbor Tam dreams the dream aloud in his presence: 'ninety-one days.' Xanthe checks the reactor logs and finds an automated shutdown sequence no one authorized. The beat is cold fear made concrete.

chapters.title: Letters Never Delivered
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She opens her brother's recovered effects: a journal describing a broadcast the founders hid inside the relay, meant to reach children 'when they were ready.' The beat is grief curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: The Scientist in Exile
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. He finds Dr. Oyelaran hiding in the outer farms; she confirms the dream is a stored transmission keyed to the next generation's neural development, and the reactor countdown will erase it forever when it completes. The beat is revelation with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: Ninety Days to Silence
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. They plan the run to Relay-0 through dead space where no rescue exists. The Council announces a 'sleep hygiene' program—drugging the children. The beat is resolve hardening against institutional denial.

chapters.title: The Garden Burns Back
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Sabotage destroys half the seed vault; the Council blames smugglers. Xanthe understands they're flushing him out. He leaves the garden he loves, knowing he may never return. The beat is sacrifice—the price begins.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The flight through the silent zone: systems failing, Ilsa confessing her real motive is her brother's last known coordinates, Xanthe admitting he's carried guilt for a delivery he abandoned years ago. The beat is intimacy forged in danger.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the First Promise
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. They find the derelict founder ship; aboard are records showing the severance between colonies was engineered by the first Council to bury the founders' confession of a terraforming failure. The beat is betrayal across generations.

chapters.title: Intercepted
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. A Council pursuit vessel corners them; Oyelaran, transmitting from Vesperine, buys them time by claiming the dream is a natural phenomenon—but is arrested. The beat is allies paying the hero's costs.

chapters.title: Seventeen Days
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Repairs under fire; Ilsa is injured shielding him. She makes him promise to finish even if she can't. The beat is loyalty tested against survival, and survival losing.

chapters.title: The Door in the Dream
chapters.summary: Tam's POV (interlude). On Vesperine, the drugged children stop dreaming—except Tam, who resists the sedative and sees the final number: seven days. The beat is innocence carrying the torch the adults dropped.

chapters.title: Relay Zero
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. They dock with the ancient relay; inside, Ilsa finds her brother's skeleton beside a terminal—he reached it first and died keeping the channel alive. The beat is devastating inheritance: someone paid before them.

chapters.title: The Founders' Voice
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. He plays the recording: the founders apologizing for poisoning the soil, begging the children not to repeat their silence, offering the truth as inheritance rather than shame. The beat is catharsis—grief transmuted into gift.

chapters.title: The Choice of Two Silences
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The Council offers amnesty if they destroy the recording; exposure means both colonies learn their peace was built on a lie. Xanthe must decide. The beat is the thematic crux—loyalty versus truth, fully armed.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. With three days left, he routes the founders' message through every relay—including Meridian's—reuniting the severed worlds in shared hearing. The Council scrambles, too late. The beat is irreversible commitment.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Arrested on return, he faces the colony expecting rage; instead the children, awake and unafraid, recite the founders' words back to the Council. The reactor countdown is cancelled. The beat is justice delivered by the inheritors themselves.

chapters.title: What Grows After
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Months later: trade resumes with Meridian, Oyelaran is freed, and the first joint expedition launches. Ilsa buries her brother's journal in restored soil. The beat is mourning braided with renewal.

chapters.title: The Garden for Everyone
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. He replants the vault, this time teaching children alongside him—Tam among them. The dream has ended; the message lives awake. Final line echoes chapter one: the garden was never for no one. The beat is quiet, earned hope.
